name: South Mumbai Heritage Walk by MDT
description:
The Mumbai Heritage Walk is a great way to experience the city’s vibrant culture and rich history.
Mumbai Heritage Walk is probably known as the ‘dream city’ and rightly so the city is indeed like a beautiful, magnificent dream. Old Mumbai is the part of Mumbai that represents its heritage and history. Reflecting on the time of Colonial era, the area is studded with numerous tourist attractions. From Chhatrapati Shivaji terminus to the ‘White town’ to the University library to the magnificent Marine drive, the city has so many spectacular attractions that one can never miss. Explore all these places of Old Mumbai and many more with this heritage walk tour.

Walking tours expose many residents and visitors to the structures.

featured_reviews.name: Ishaan Srivastav
featured_reviews.review_text: We had the pleasure of taking the inside CSMT (Crown Jewel of Mumbai) tour with Sarthak Mahajan, and he was exceptional. Sarthak is incredibly knowledgeable, seamlessly weaving together stories of the building’s storied past with insights into its present-day operations. His passion for the history of the station is evident, and he made the entire walk a very pleasant, fun and engaging experience. Highly recommended for anyone looking to truly understand the soul of this UNESCO World Heritage site!

featured_reviews.name: Carol Thomson
featured_reviews.review_text:
The CST tour was a great experience.
It really felt like stepping into a whole different world full of history and amazing architecture.

Our guide, Sarthak, was exceptional. He eloquently walked us through the evolution of Indian Railways and the fascinating story behind CST, bringing every detail to life.
He also took us to all the best spots, which made it even better.

The architecture is just beautiful and so diverse—you can really see why it’s a UNESCO World Heritage site.

Overall, it was a memorable time and I’m really grateful to Sarthak for all the insights and knowledge that he shared.

featured_reviews.name: Liviu-Alexandru Buftea (Style)
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you found this place, you had a good guide!

I thought it was Portuguese, but it's actually British. Black as the basaltic rock that rises from the sea, Worli Fort gives a great overview of the bay and the city. It features the classic crenelations and ramparts of the 17th century, and guards the golf from the tip of this tongue of land.

The fort now is not officially maintained or "open to the public". In fact, it seems even locals don’t know about it, but my friend brought me here cause she heard it’s nice. It is accessible for explorer types, and is basically left abandoned.

The fort is simply used by people in this neighborhood for storage, hang out, kids play space, etc. Some clothes left out to dry on the sides, and some barrels and stuff in the rooms below.

Here we met a couple of guys from the city, chilling, listening to cool music, they welcomed us to chat.

It smelled of sea salt, soap, garbage, fish and rats, and the breeze brought “fresh” air from the sea.

As a first time visitor in India, I was in culture shock. Seeing everything was kind of like a dreamy, surreal landscape. So I probably romanticized it too much, for the place is a slum surrounded by a garbage dump, and people here have little chance to better their days, but they were happy, kind and curious.

It was an interesting and humbling experience, worth respect.

featured_reviews.review_text: This is the one of the best place to have mumbai's view, only drawback I noticed was connectivity from metro, etc, still it is walkable if alone or not with family, you will have to cross koliwada but the road is good must go in good rainy weather clear sunset time.

featured_reviews.name: Hr Patil
featured_reviews.review_text: Worli Fort and Worli Koliwada offer a beautiful mix of Mumbai’s history, culture, and sea views. The fort gives a peaceful vibe with stunning views of the Bandra-Worli Sea Link, especially during sunset. The narrow lanes of Worli Koliwada showcase the authentic charm of Mumbai’s fishing community and local lifestyle. It’s a great place for photography, exploring hidden corners of the city, and enjoying calm moments away from the busy streets. The atmosphere feels raw, real, and deeply connected to Mumbai’s heritage. Definitely worth visiting if you enjoy historic places and scenic coastal views.

featured_reviews.name: Amit Gurav
featured_reviews.review_text:

The fort remains completely closed; access is possible only from the Dargah side. Many walls and structural portions have fallen, highlighting the critical state of decay.

featured_reviews.name: Tasmiya Shiledar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mahim Fort, located in the Mahim area of Mumbai, is one of the lesser-known historical sites in the city. Built by the Portuguese in the 16th century, it originally served as a strategic military outpost. However, over time, the fort fell into disrepair and now exists in a somewhat dilapidated state, making it less of a tourist attraction compared to other forts in Mumbai like Gateway of India or Bandra Fort.

### Key Aspects:
1. **Historical Significance**: The fort was originally constructed by the Portuguese in 1680 to defend the area from the Marathas. It was later taken over by the British in the 18th century. It’s interesting from a historical standpoint, though not much of the original structure remains intact.

2. **Location**: Mahim Fort is located near the Mahim Beach, which is a busy part of Mumbai. The fort itself is tucked away in a residential area, which means it’s not a prominent tourist spot and can sometimes be overlooked.

3. **Condition**: The fort is in poor condition and lacks proper maintenance. Most of the fort’s structure is reduced to ruins, and it’s surrounded by modern buildings. It doesn't offer the same panoramic views or grandeur as other forts, which can make it less appealing to those looking for a more scenic or fully preserved historical experience.

4. **Accessibility**: The fort is accessible to the public, but you’ll likely need to search for it amidst local streets and residential buildings. It’s not as well-marked as other historical sites in Mumbai, so visiting may require a little bit of patience and exploration.

5. **Cultural Context**: While the fort itself may not be a major draw for tourists, the area around it offers a glimpse into the local life of Mumbai, with its mix of residential homes and bustling markets. It’s a good place to experience the contrast between Mumbai's rich history and its modern-day hustle and bustle.

### Overall Review:
Mahim Fort can be an interesting visit for history buffs or those looking to explore off-the-beaten-path locations in Mumbai. However, if you're expecting a well-preserved, tourist-friendly fort, you might be disappointed. It's a quiet spot, perfect for those looking for a peaceful break from the busy city, but it's not a must-see if you're short on time.

featured_reviews.name: Milind Kocharekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mahim Fort is the oldest fort in Mumbai. Connecting the east-west coasts of Mumbai and guarding the bay of Mahim, this fort was known as the gatekeeper of the waterway. At the mouth of the Mahikavati aka Mahim bay, which separates the islands of Mumbai from the mainland, Pratap Bimba Raja built the Mahim fort in 1140 AD and established his capital there. And by calling people doing various types of business, trade, enterprise, science And the seeds of culture were planted on the island of Mumbai.
After the fort came under the control of the British, the English architect Jerrold Augier rebuilt the existing fort. In 1672 AD, the Portuguese attacked the fort of Mahim. At that time the fort was equipped with 100 soldiers and 30 guns; So the Portuguese could not conquer it. Then on 14 February 1689 Siddhi Yakut Khan of Janjira attacked Mumbai with 2500 soldiers. At that time, after conquering the fort of Mahim, he ravaged the area for a year, looting
Protected by strong fortifications and bastions on all sides, the entrance of this fort stands as a testimony of British architecture. The crafts on it and the raised pillars on both sides can be seen. Due to encroachment in the fort, nothing else can be seen.
Mahim fort on the sea can be reached in 10 minutes if you get off at Mahim (West) station on the Western Railway and walk towards Mahim beach along Mori Road.

You can see walls of Fort from Sea side but from city no one can know whether we have such Fort in this locality.

featured_reviews.name: Derishta Pillay
featured_reviews.review_text:
At the outset I must say that neither myself nor my husband are huge fans of the usual guided walking tours mainly because we hate being taken to cliched and crowded tourist hotspots, listening to facts straight from the Wikipedia page and jostling for space with other tourists just to return sunburned and underwhelmed. In addition we'd already spent a hectic 5 weeks in India - we were tired, grumpy, waiting to fly back home and not at all looking forward to our last 4 days in Mumbai at all. So basically when our travel companions insisted we book a tour - the scene was set for disaster...
'Bombay Walks' single handedly turned this around and Mumbai actually turned out to be the highlight of our trip! (Nope this is not a sponsored review 😂)

The tour: Arpan's tour extends to the days before and after the actual tour as he offers valuable advice about where to stay/eat/party/shop etc. He speaks perfect English, is pleasant and very easy to communicate with. His passion and love for the city is infectious and you will end his tour enthralled, overwhelmed and completely charmed by Mumbai and it's people - vowing to come back and dig deeper, spend longer and see more. The city tour covers many facets of the city - traveling to hidden gems and local landmarks across the length and breadth of Mumbai. You get to see and experience aspects of Mumbai that you'd never be able to do alone with a guide book or google maps - like traveling on local trains and walking through Worli fishing village and stopping by at small off-the-beaten path temples and churches.

The guide: Arpan is reliable, trustworthy and comes well prepared for the type of group. His talking style is light-hearted and easy going but still knowledgeable and always engaging. He's the type of guide that can tell you interesting facts about the history, architecture and politics of a place but also where to get the best coconut water along the way and which public toilets are ok to use.
We only met Arpan in person on the day of the tour and although we were constantly bombarded with sights, sounds and smells (it is Mumbai after all) - it never once felt like we were just being dragged from point to point whilst he rattled off information but rather that we were spending the day walking around with an old friend.

Target travelers: We're fairly well travelled and yet this is the first time we've ever bothered to leave a tour review - on any platform - I think that in itself indicates how highly we recommend this tour.
This is really a 'must do' in Mumbai.
It's so good we would do this tour again even if it were to cover the exact route we already took. The walking wasn't particular strenuous so it's recommended for any age group it should also be noted that we found that     Arpan was discreetly always conscious of where the group members were and their safety and constantly aware of our surroundings and the locals around us - on that note I would recommend this tour even if you're a single female traveling alone.

When to do it: Try and do this tour on your first full day in Mumbai because it's also a great way to orientate yourself around the city and plan the rest of your time there.

That city that everyone talks about - that's all of India's many faces and layers in one, that accepts everyone, that's everyone's home - regardless of language, religion or creed - Mumbai is THAT city and you'd be crazy if you miss the opportunity to let a born-and-bred local guide you around...

featured_reviews.name: shoeb sayed
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jogger’s Park is one of Mumbai’s most beloved seaside urban parks and jogging spots, nestled at the southern end of Carter Road promenade in Bandra West. It’s a classic example of how community initiative transformed a former garbage dump into a green fitness haven in the early 1990s, thanks largely to local efforts led by Oliver Andrade and support from prominent Mumbai residents — a legacy memorialised by a plaque at the entrance that says “From Sir, With Love.”
Wikipedia

Park Highlights
Scenic jogging tracks: The park features a 400-metre long stretch with a mix of mud, synthetic and paved pathways that suit casual walkers and serious runners alike.

Sea views & fresh air: Its location along the Arabian Sea offers cool breezes and calming views of the water — especially beautiful at sunrise and sunset.
Chalbanjare
Green spaces & gardens: Beyond jogging, there are lush lawns, landscaped paths, benches and shaded spots perfect for relaxation, meditation, or reading.
Chalbanjare
Kid-friendly area: There’s a dedicated children’s play area with swings, slides and soft flooring, making it family-friendly.
The Indian Express

Activities & Atmosphere
Jogger’s Park isn’t just for fitness — it’s a community hub where locals gather for morning runs, evening walks, yoga sessions or simply to meet friends. It’s also known for hosting Mumbai’s first laughter club, a unique wellness activity that began here.

Visitors often enjoy:
Walking or running with sea views
Meditation and casual outdoor workouts
Relaxing on benches overlooking the coast
Family outings with kids in the play area

Practical Info
Timings: Typically open 5:00 AM – 9:00 PM (best early morning and evening).
Whats Hot
Entry: Free to enter since the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) took over maintenance.  
Ticket Fairy
Location: At the end of Carter Road, near landmarks like Otters Club and Bandra’s lively seafront promenade.  
Ticket Fairy
Getting there: Easily reachable by auto/taxi from Bandra Railway Station, or by BEST buses along Carter Road.
Ticket Fairy

Jogger’s Park blends fitness with serenity a rare open space in a bustling city where you can breathe fresh sea air, watch waves crash, and enjoy a peaceful escape without leaving the suburb. Locals and visitors alike cherish it for its history, community vibe, and relaxed seaside ambience.

featured_reviews.name: Note from Travelam
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had an amazing experience with Mumbai Dream Tours! A special thanks to Hardhik, who made this journey truly memorable with his incredible knowledge, guidance, and hospitality throughout the tour.

The 3-hour trek was one of the most unique experiences in Mumbai, covering iconic places like the world’s largest open-air laundry at Dhobi Ghat, the fascinating Dabbawala system, and the vibrant life of Dharavi. Hardhik explained every detail with so much passion and insight, making the entire experience engaging and meaningful.

What stood out the most was how comfortable and well-guided we felt throughout the tour. It was not just sightseeing, but a real understanding of Mumbai’s culture, people, and hardworking spirit.

Highly recommended for anyone visiting Mumbai and wanting to explore the city beyond the usual tourist spots. Thank you once again, Hardhik and Mumbai Dream Tours, for such a wonderful experience!

featured_reviews.name: Danna Katzman
featured_reviews.review_text: We went on the Dharavi Slum Tour with Rakesh as our guide. It was intense, overwhelming, and inspiring all at once. Rakesh was wonderful - very knowledgeable and willing to answer all our many questions. He took us through the bustling commercial area first and then we also saw a crowded residential area. This tour really makes you think about ones own privilege, the ways many people in this world have to live, and the how they find opportunities to thrive. Highly recommend this tour.

featured_reviews.name: Felicitas
featured_reviews.review_text:
The tour with Abhi was one of the absolute highlights of my time in Mumbai: insightful, respectful and so much more than a typical city tour. Abhi guides you through Dhobi Ghat and Dharavi with calmness and authenticity, explains social and economic contexts, shares stories from the community and manages to convey a complex reality. I learned so many new things!
Also I felt safe and well taken care of at all times, and the tour genuinely moved me. If you’re looking for a tour that not only provides information but also real insight and connection, Abhi is the perfect guide.

I would happily use this tour company again should I return to Mumbai.
